text: With an average of 4,500 pedestrians per hour, Yonge Street and Eglinton Avenue is one of the busiest pedestrian intersections in Toronto. As the local community is keenly aware, pedestrian congestion extends well beyond the intersection and into the surrounding neighborhood. With the long-awaited opening of the Eglinton Crosstown LRT, it is time to reimagine the Yonge and Eglinton corridor to better serve the tens of thousands of pedestrians who navigate the crossings every day. This motion recommends the installation of a pedestrian priority phase, also known as a “pedestrian scramble,” at two intersections: Yonge Street and Eglinton Avenue, and Roehampton Avenue and Orchard View Boulevard. City Council on July 29 and 30, 2026, adopted the following: 1. City Council request the General Manager, Transportation Services to proceed with detailed design and operational analysis for a Pedestrian Priority Phase at Yonge Street and Eglinton Avenue to be implemented in 2027, subject to consideration through the 2027 budget process and Council approval of the funding and resource requirements, taking into account other City priorities. 2. City Council request the General Manager, Transportation Services to evaluate the implementation of an exclusive pedestrian phase at Yonge Street and Roehampton Avenue/Orchard View Boulevard to be implemented in 2027 as part of the same initiative, subject to consideration through the 2027 budget process and Council approval of the funding and resource requirements, taking into account other City priorities. 3.
